To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell surface marker profiles of neural stem cells, glia, and neurons derived from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) are similar to those of their native counterparts, and that a panel of cell surface marker antibodies can be used for the isolation of these cell types.
we have identified cell-surface marker signatures for the isolation of neural stem cells (NSC), neurons, and glia from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs).

we developed a novel method to identify cell-surface marker profiles of human neural stem cells, astrocytes and neurons derived from human pluripotent stem cells, and applied the method to identify a set of 11 cell-surface markers that are suitable for the isolation of neural stem cells, glia and neurons.

the development of novel, efficient, and cost-effective strategies for the generation of functional neurons and glial cells from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) for cell-based therapies and in vitro disease models.
the study of the mechanisms of the development of the nervous system, in particular the development of the brain, and with the study of neurodegenerative diseases.
the isolation and characterization of neural cells from pluripotent stem cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of human stem cells in research has a great potential to improve our understanding of human biology and disease, but it also has a potential to cause harm, which needs to be considered.

the human pluripotent stem cells can be differentiated to neural lineages, including neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes, and these cells have the potential to be used for cell-based therapies for neurological diseases.

the use of the human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs)-derived neural cells in research and development of novel therapeutics for neurodegenerative disorders and other neurological diseases has been limited due to the lack of efficient and robust protocols for the generation of hPSCs-derived neuronal subtypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a series of cell surface marker-based protocols for the isolation and enrichment of neural stem cells (NSC), glia and neurons from human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs).
we have developed cell surface marker signatures for the isolation of human pluripotent stem cell derived neural stem cells, glia and neurons.
we have developed a method for the isolation of neural stem cells and glia from pluripotent stem cell cultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs) for the production of neural cells in vitro is an attractive alternative for the study of neural development, disease, and drug discovery.

there is a significant difference between the cell surface markers of human pluripotent stem cell derived neural cells and their mouse counterparts, which is a result of the evolutionary divergence of human and mouse neural cells.
there is no single cell-surface marker that is specific to human neural stem cells (NSCs), glia, or neurons, but rather, a combination of markers is required to enrich for each of these populations.
